agenda.2026-11-16-japon-pib-troisieme-tr: Japan: first estimate of third-quarter growth

The Japanese government publishes its first estimate of July-September GDP on Monday, November 16 [1][2]. Second-quarter growth was revised up to an annualized 1.4% [3]: the figure will show whether the Japanese economy is keeping up that pace.
agenda.2026-11-19-afrique-du-sud-banque-: South Africa: the central bank sets its policy rate

The South African Reserve Bank announces its last rate decision of the year on November 19 [1]. Nedbank economists expect a 0.25-point hike [2]: borrowing would become more expensive for South African households and businesses.
agenda.2026-11-19-walmart-resultats.why: The US retail giant reports on Thursday, November 19, before Wall Street opens [1]. It is aiming for adjusted earnings of $0.62 to $0.64 per share and sales growth of 3% to 3.75% at constant exchange rates [2]: a gauge of American consumer spending ahead of the holidays.
agenda.2026-11-24-portugal-budget-2027-v: Portugal: final vote on the 2027 budget

Portugal's parliament votes on the 2027 budget as a whole on November 24, after the article-by-article review [1][2]. At first reading, on October 28, the bill passed with the votes of the PSD and CDS-PP and the abstention of the Socialist Party [1].
agenda.2026-12-01-zone-euro-inflation-no: Euro area: flash estimate of November inflation

Eurostat publishes its flash estimate of November price growth on December 1 [1][2]. In October, inflation reached 4.0%, its highest level in three years [3]: it is the last major figure before the ECB meeting on December 17.
agenda.2026-12-04-etats-unis-emploi-nove: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes November job creation and the unemployment rate on Friday, December 4, at 8:30 a.m. Washington time [1]. In October, the economy added 165,000 jobs and unemployment fell to 4.1% [2]; it is the last report before the Fed meeting on December 8 and 9.
Gambians elect their president on Saturday, December 5, a date set by the Independent Electoral Commission [1][2]. Incumbent president Adama Barrow is seeking a third term, although he had initially pledged to serve only one [3].
